prompt.context_jp: 昼どきの喫茶店には、コーヒーの香りと油の匂い___薄く漂っていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: コーヒーの香りと油の匂い（　）薄く漂っていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that introduces the scene's new descriptive detail.

feedback.correct_en: The narrator is painting a scene for the first time — the smells are brand-new information the reader is being shown, so が marks them as the just-noticed subject.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would treat the smells as an already-established topic being commented on, which doesn't fit an opening scene-setting sentence. を can't mark the subject of 漂う.

contrast_examples.jp: 部屋にコーヒーの香りが漂っている。
contrast_examples.en: The smell of coffee is drifting through the room. (presenting the scene)

contrast_examples.jp: コーヒーの香りは、やっぱりいいね。
contrast_examples.en: That coffee smell — it really is nice. (commenting on a known topic)

prompt.context_jp: 圭介が白石の母に打ち明ける場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「万理華さん（　）私の妻の生まれ変わりなんです」
prompt.prompt_en: Keisuke makes his biggest claim about Marika. Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: Marika is already the known person both speakers are discussing; Keisuke is making a claim ABOUT her. That topic-comment structure takes は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would frame Marika as newly-identified new information (as in answering 'who is the reincarnation?'), but here Marika is the given topic and 'is my wife's reincarnation' is the new comment.

contrast_examples.jp: 万理華さんは私の妻の生まれ変わりです。
contrast_examples.en: As for Marika — she is my wife's reincarnation. (comment about a known person)

contrast_examples.jp: 生まれ変わりは万理華さんです。
contrast_examples.en: The reincarnated one is Marika. (identifying who, exhaustive が-type context)

prompt.context_jp: 妻のことを初めて紹介する圭介。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「私の妻（　）新島貴恵といいます」
prompt.prompt_en: Keisuke introduces his wife by name. Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: This is a classic 'as for X, X is called Y' topic-comment introduction. The wife is the topic being described, so は is natural.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would sound like he's picking his wife out of a set to answer 'which one is Niijima Takie?' — not the situation here.

contrast_examples.jp: 私の妻は新島貴恵といいます。
contrast_examples.en: My wife is called Niijima Takie. (introducing/defining a topic)

contrast_examples.jp: 新島貴恵というのが私の妻です。
contrast_examples.en: The one called Niijima Takie is my wife. (identificational が)

prompt.context_jp: 食卓に、ふいに割り込むような声がした。
prompt.prompt_jp: 貴恵の弟の友利（　）、いつのまにか椅子を引き寄せて、二人の様子を横目でにらんでいた。
prompt.prompt_en: A new person appears on the scene. Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: Tomori is being introduced into the scene for the first time here — pure new-information が. The reader is 'noticing' him sitting there.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would presuppose Tomori as a continuing topic, but he's just now entering the narrative frame.

contrast_examples.jp: 弟の友利が椅子を引き寄せていた。
contrast_examples.en: His younger brother Tomori had pulled up a chair. (new participant)

contrast_examples.jp: 友利は、いつも二人を横目で見ている。
contrast_examples.en: Tomori always watches the two of them sideways. (habitual comment about a known topic)

prompt.context_jp: 母親についての思い出が話題に。
prompt.prompt_jp: 貴恵（　）生前、母親のことをほとんど口にしなかった。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle that establishes Takie as the sentence's topic.

feedback.correct_en: Takie is already the central figure of the family's thoughts; the sentence is making a general statement about her habit. は fits a known topic + commentary.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make this sound like Takie is being singled out from alternatives ('it was Takie — not someone else — who didn't talk about her mother'), which isn't the point here.

contrast_examples.jp: 貴恵は母親のことを話さなかった。
contrast_examples.en: Takie didn't talk about her mother. (statement about Takie)

contrast_examples.jp: 貴恵が話さなかった(=誰だ？貴恵だ)。
contrast_examples.en: The one who didn't talk was Takie. (exhaustive identification)

prompt.context_jp: 貴恵が最近つぶやいた内容を圭介が引用する場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「貴恵が言ってたんだ 今のお母さん（　）自分の母親に似てるって」
prompt.prompt_en: Keisuke quotes what Takie said. Which particle fits inside the quoted claim?

feedback.correct_en: Inside a subordinate 〜って clause describing a resemblance observation, the subject typically takes が. The content is new information being reported.
feedback.incorrect_en: は inside this embedded clause would wrench the topic out of the main sentence; here 'the current mother' is a fresh subject being compared, not a running topic.

contrast_examples.jp: 今のお母さんが自分の母親に似てる、と貴恵が言った。
contrast_examples.en: Takie said the current mother resembles her own mother. (new embedded subject → が)

contrast_examples.jp: 今のお母さんは、優しい人だ。
contrast_examples.en: The current mother is a kind person. (main-clause topic)

prompt.context_jp: 実家に帰る理由を話す場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「母（　）夫婦ゲンカしたみたいで ちょっとモメてるみたい」
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits in this report of a fresh event?

feedback.correct_en: This is reporting a one-off event ('mom apparently got into a fight'). New-event subjects inside subordinate 〜みたいで clauses take が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would frame mom as the ongoing topic and sound like a general statement about her, not a fresh incident being reported.

contrast_examples.jp: 母が夫婦ゲンカしたみたい。
contrast_examples.en: Apparently mom got into a fight. (reporting a new event)

contrast_examples.jp: 母は、よく父とケンカする。
contrast_examples.en: Mom often fights with Dad. (habitual topic-comment)

prompt.context_jp: のほほんと話す貴恵の一言。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「いいじゃないの 平和（　）いちばんよ」
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits in 'peace is the best'?

feedback.correct_en: 〜がいちばん is a fixed exhaustive-listing pattern: of all possibilities, X is the one that's best. が picks out the exclusive winner.
feedback.incorrect_en: 平和はいちばん sounds unnatural here — it loses the sense of singling peace out above every alternative.

contrast_examples.jp: 健康がいちばんだ。
contrast_examples.en: Health is the most important. (exhaustive 〜がいちばん)

contrast_examples.jp: 健康は大事だ。
contrast_examples.en: Health is important. (general topic-comment)

prompt.context_jp: 白石が娘にぶつけた言葉の記憶。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「あんた（　）いなければ あんな男と結婚なんか…」
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits in this conditional?

feedback.correct_en: In 〜がいなければ / 〜がなければ conditionals, the subject of existence takes が. The mother is picking out her daughter as the specific cause.
feedback.incorrect_en: あんたはいなければ is ungrammatical — は can't normally sit inside a conditional existence clause this way.

contrast_examples.jp: あんたがいなければ、こうならなかった。
contrast_examples.en: If you hadn't existed, this wouldn't have happened.

contrast_examples.jp: お金がなければ、生きられない。
contrast_examples.en: If there were no money, we couldn't live.

prompt.context_jp: 麻衣に怒られた話を思い出して。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「ママに怒られてから（　）なるべく自炊してたからな」
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits after the 〜てから time clause?

feedback.correct_en: 〜てからは contrasts 'the period after X' with 'before X' — implicit contrast with their old habits. は gives that 'since then (as opposed to before)' nuance.
feedback.incorrect_en: が doesn't attach to adverbial 〜てから clauses this way; it needs a subject, not a time frame.

contrast_examples.jp: 結婚してからは、自炊するようになった。
contrast_examples.en: Since getting married, I've started cooking at home (as opposed to before).

contrast_examples.jp: 結婚してから、十年経った。
contrast_examples.en: Ten years have passed since getting married. (neutral time reference)

prompt.context_jp: 白石が席を立って帰るところ。
prompt.prompt_jp: 白石の背中（　）店を出ていくと、店内の空気が急にゆるんだ。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits in this subordinate 〜と clause?

feedback.correct_en: Subjects of subordinate 〜と / 〜ば / 〜たら clauses almost always take が. The back disappearing out the door is a concrete triggering event.
feedback.incorrect_en: は inside a 〜と temporal clause would feel like it's trying to be a main-clause topic — the structure doesn't allow it here.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼が帰ると、みんなほっとした。
contrast_examples.en: When he left, everyone felt relieved. (subordinate が)

contrast_examples.jp: 彼は帰った。みんなほっとした。
contrast_examples.en: He went home. Everyone felt relieved. (main-clause は)

prompt.context_jp: 母のことを話したがらなかった貴恵。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「貴恵は 自分の母親のこと（　）あまり話してくれなかったから」
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks the implicit contrast ('her mother, specifically')?

feedback.correct_en: This は on the object sets up a contrast: 'other things she'd talk about, but her mother — not much.' The sentence quietly implies that limited topic.
feedback.incorrect_en: を would be grammatical but flat; は carries the key contrastive nuance ('as for THIS subject matter'). が doesn't fit a direct object slot here.

contrast_examples.jp: 父のことはよく話したが、母のことはあまり話さなかった。
contrast_examples.en: She talked a lot about her father, but about her mother, not so much. (contrast は)

contrast_examples.jp: 母のことを話した。
contrast_examples.en: She spoke about her mother. (neutral object)

prompt.context_jp: お弁当の話を聞いた瞬間。
prompt.prompt_jp: 圭介の言葉に、白石の脳裏（　）ひとつの光景がよぎった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks the path/space the scene crosses?

feedback.correct_en: よぎる takes を to mark the space traversed. A scene 'crosses through' her mind — a traversal object marked by を.
feedback.incorrect_en: に would mark a static destination, not a passing-through motion. が would make 脳裏 the subject, but the subject here is 光景.

contrast_examples.jp: 不安が頭をよぎった。
contrast_examples.en: Anxiety flashed through my head. (traversal を)

contrast_examples.jp: 頭に不安が浮かんだ。
contrast_examples.en: Anxiety surfaced in my head. (static location に)

prompt.context_jp: お弁当を作っていた朝の記憶。
prompt.prompt_jp: 娘が朝早く起きて、慣れない手つきで台所（　）立っていた、あの日のことだった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks the place where the daughter was standing?

feedback.correct_en: 立つ is a verb of existence/posture, and location of existence/posture takes に. 台所に立つ is the fixed pattern for 'to be standing in the kitchen (cooking).'
feedback.incorrect_en: で marks the location of an action in progress, but 立っていた here describes being-in-a-posture, not performing an action — so に is natural.

contrast_examples.jp: 台所に立っていた。
contrast_examples.en: She was standing in the kitchen. (posture/existence)

contrast_examples.jp: 台所で料理していた。
contrast_examples.en: She was cooking in the kitchen. (dynamic action)

prompt.context_jp: 喫茶店で向かい合う圭介。
prompt.prompt_jp: 娘のことで話がある——そうLINEで前置きしておいた圭介の顔に（　）、緊張が張りついている。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle lets us focus on 'his face in particular'?

feedback.correct_en: に + は zooms in on the face as the specific location bearing tension — a classic 'as for his face' narrative framing.
feedback.incorrect_en: 顔が緊張が張りついている can't have two が on the same clause; and simply にが is ungrammatical.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼の顔には、疲れがにじんでいた。
contrast_examples.en: On his face, exhaustion was showing. (focused location)

contrast_examples.jp: 彼の顔に汗が浮かんだ。
contrast_examples.en: Sweat formed on his face. (neutral location に)

prompt.context_jp: 喫茶店で誰と誰が会っていたのかの叙述。
prompt.prompt_jp: 向かい合ったの（　）、あの新島圭介と、白石万理華の母だった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits in this cleft-style identification?

feedback.correct_en: 〜のは〜だ is the standard cleft/pseudo-cleft pattern. The nominalized 'the ones who faced each other' is the topic, and the names are the comment.
feedback.incorrect_en: 〜のが〜 exists in some contexts but doesn't fit the 'the ones who X were Y' identificational cleft structure the narrator is using here.

contrast_examples.jp: 来たのは田中さんだった。
contrast_examples.en: The one who came was Mr. Tanaka. (cleft は)

contrast_examples.jp: 田中さんが来た。
contrast_examples.en: Mr. Tanaka came. (plain new-info が)

prompt.context_jp: 日々の些細な出来事の積み重ねが貴恵という存在を形づくっていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 塵も（　）山となるというが、日々の些細な出来事の積み重ねこそが…
prompt.prompt_en: Complete the proverb.

feedback.correct_en: 塵も積もれば山となる is the fixed proverb — 'even dust, if it piles up, becomes a mountain.' Keisuke invokes it to describe accumulated small moments.
feedback.incorrect_en: 降る (to fall) and 飛ぶ (to fly) break the imagery and the fixed phrase. Only 積もれば gives the 'accumulate' meaning the proverb requires.

contrast_examples.jp: 塵も積もれば山となる。
contrast_examples.en: Many a little makes a mickle.

contrast_examples.jp: 小さな努力も積もれば大きな成果になる。
contrast_examples.en: Even small efforts, when accumulated, become great results.

prompt.context_jp: 相手の警戒を解こうとして、彼は何度も…
prompt.prompt_jp: 彼は何度も言葉を（　）。
prompt.prompt_en: Keisuke carefully rechoses his words.

feedback.correct_en: 〜直す means 'to redo' — 選び直す = 'to choose again, re-pick.' That captures his repeated reselection to find the right wording.
feedback.incorrect_en: 選び終えた means 'finished choosing' (one-shot completion). 選ばなかった means 'didn't choose,' the opposite of the described action.

contrast_examples.jp: 言葉を選び直す。
contrast_examples.en: to reword / re-pick one's phrasing

contrast_examples.jp: やり直す。
contrast_examples.en: to redo (compound with 〜直す)

prompt.context_jp: 貴恵が圭介をからかう。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「あなたみたいに 幸せな家庭で（　）育った人には 一生 分かんないから」
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the adverb that captures 'carefree, naively.'

feedback.correct_en: のほほんと describes carefree, unworried ease — exactly the gentle teasing Takie aims at Keisuke's sheltered upbringing.
feedback.incorrect_en: ぴりぴり evokes nervous tension — the opposite nuance. どしどし means 'briskly / in large numbers,' which doesn't fit describing a personality.

contrast_examples.jp: のほほんと暮らす。
contrast_examples.en: to live in a carefree way

contrast_examples.jp: ぴりぴりしている。
contrast_examples.en: to be on edge / tense

prompt.context_jp: 友利が母のことを語る。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「過剰に相手に期待して それで 裏切られたって（　）って まあ それの繰り返し」
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the casual verb for 'to flip out / get hysterical.'

feedback.correct_en: ヒスる is slangy, from 'hysteria' — to lose control emotionally. Tomori uses this casual register to describe his mother's outbursts.
feedback.incorrect_en: ホッとする = feel relieved. ワクワクする = feel excited. Neither matches the mother's angry breakdowns.

contrast_examples.jp: 母ちゃんがまたヒスってる。
contrast_examples.en: Mom is losing it again. (casual)

contrast_examples.jp: 母はまた取り乱している。
contrast_examples.en: Mom is getting agitated again. (neutral)

prompt.context_jp: 姉は母を怒らせないように気を配っていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: そんな母ちゃんの空気（　）、イライラさせないように先回りして明るくして…
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the verb that forms 'to read the atmosphere.'

feedback.correct_en: 空気を読む is the fixed collocation — 'to read the room / sense the mood.' Tomori describes his sister as highly attuned to their mother's moods.
feedback.incorrect_en: 見る or 聞く break the idiom; neither carries the sense of intuiting unspoken emotional atmosphere.

contrast_examples.jp: 空気を読む。
contrast_examples.en: to read the atmosphere

contrast_examples.jp: 空気が読めない。
contrast_examples.en: He can't read the room. (socially tone-deaf)

prompt.context_jp: 娘を失ったと悟った母の叫び。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「万理華を（　）！」
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the verb that fits a desperate 'give her back!'

feedback.correct_en: 返す = 'to return (a thing/person to the owner).' The mother is demanding her daughter be given back to her, so 返して is the fit.
feedback.incorrect_en: 帰す means 'to send someone home,' which shifts the meaning away from 'give her back to me.' 戻って is intransitive — 'come back' — and can't take 万理華を as object.

contrast_examples.jp: 娘を返して！
contrast_examples.en: Give my daughter back! (demand return of possession)

contrast_examples.jp: もう遅いから、子どもを家に帰した。
contrast_examples.en: It was late, so I sent the child home. (dismiss someone homeward)

prompt.context_jp: 圭介が白石の母に打ち明ける。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「謝らなきゃいけないことが お母さんに ちゃんと（　）彼女と会ってました」
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the humble form fitting the apology.

feedback.correct_en: お〜する is humble language, and 〜せずに = 'without doing.' Keisuke apologizes for meeting Marika 'without properly having told you first.'
feedback.incorrect_en: 伝えてから means 'after telling' — the opposite situation. 伝えたくて ('wanting to tell') makes no sense in this apology.

contrast_examples.jp: ご連絡せずに申し訳ありません。
contrast_examples.en: I'm sorry for not having contacted you. (humble + 〜ずに)

contrast_examples.jp: お伝えしてから伺います。
contrast_examples.en: I'll notify you first, then come. (future action)

prompt.context_jp: 白石の母が店を出た後の圭介の心境。
prompt.prompt_jp: うまく（　）とは、とても言えない。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the verb for 'to get across / be conveyed.'

feedback.correct_en: 伝わる (intransitive) focuses on whether the message reached and landed with the listener. Keisuke doubts whether his point got through.
feedback.incorrect_en: 伝えた (transitive) just means he spoke — but the question here is whether it registered. 届いた typically refers to physical objects/notices, not meaning.

contrast_examples.jp: 気持ちが伝わった。
contrast_examples.en: My feelings got through to her. (intransitive, result-focused)

contrast_examples.jp: 気持ちを伝えた。
contrast_examples.en: I conveyed my feelings. (my action)

prompt.context_jp: 圭介が切り出す場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「偽りなく 本当のことを お伝え（　）と思っています」
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the polite humble ending Keisuke uses.

feedback.correct_en: お〜する is the humble pattern; お伝えしたい = 'I wish to (humbly) tell you.' Keisuke stays in polite register when speaking to Marika's mother.
feedback.incorrect_en: お〜される is passive/honorific, so it would mean 'to be told' — wrong direction. お伝えできる means 'can tell,' which doesn't match 〜と思っています expressing intent.

contrast_examples.jp: 本当のことをお伝えしたいと思います。
contrast_examples.en: I'd like to convey the truth. (humble intent)

contrast_examples.jp: 本当のことを言いたい。
contrast_examples.en: I want to say the truth. (plain)

prompt.context_jp: 圭介の長い前置きを遮る白石の母。
prompt.prompt_en: Which line better captures the mother's cold impatience as she cuts Keisuke off?

choices.text: A: 前置きはいいです。話って何なんですか？
B: 恐れ入りますが、ご用件を伺ってもよろしいでしょうか？

feedback.correct_en: A is the clipped, flatly dismissive register the mother actually uses — 丁寧 on the surface but ending in sharp 何なんですか？ to force him to the point.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is too silky and business-polite; it suggests warmth and openness, which doesn't match a wary stranger meeting a man making an impossible claim about her daughter.

contrast_examples.jp: 前置きはいいです。
contrast_examples.en: Skip the preamble. (brusque)

contrast_examples.jp: 恐れ入ります、ご用件を…
contrast_examples.en: Pardon me, your business is…? (deferential)

prompt.context_jp: 実家に帰る貴恵（万理華の姿で）に、圭介が同行を申し出る場面。
prompt.prompt_en: Which reply sounds more natural for Takie casually brushing Keisuke off here?

choices.text: A: いいわよ、面倒くさい。
B: 結構でございます、ご面倒をおかけしますので。

feedback.correct_en: A fits the wife-and-husband intimacy. いいわよ + 面倒くさい is relaxed, slightly bossy wifely tone — exactly how Takie talks to Keisuke.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is business-level keigo. Between spouses it would sound sarcastic or alienated, which clashes with the warm teasing of this scene.

contrast_examples.jp: いいわよ、面倒くさい。
contrast_examples.en: Nah, it'd be a hassle. (intimate casual)

contrast_examples.jp: 結構でございます。
contrast_examples.en: No thank you. (formal to a stranger)

prompt.context_jp: 万理華（貴恵）が母親に静かに言い放つ場面。
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds more natural as a quiet, firm rebuke from a daughter to her mother?

choices.text: A: 子供が黙って聞いてるからって、何も感じてないわけじゃないのよ。
B: 子供が黙って聞いてるのに、何かを感じていると限らないのよ。

feedback.correct_en: 〜からって、〜わけじゃない is the natural pattern for 'just because X doesn't mean Y isn't the case' — a strong, idiomatic counter to the mother's assumption.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is grammatically patched together but doesn't flow — 〜のに〜と限らない is unnatural phrasing here and loses the force of the retort.

contrast_examples.jp: 若いからって、何でもできるわけじゃない。
contrast_examples.en: Just because you're young doesn't mean you can do everything.

contrast_examples.jp: 静かだからって、怒ってないわけじゃない。
contrast_examples.en: Just because they're quiet doesn't mean they're not angry.

prompt.context_jp: 圭介が白石の母を「お母さん」と呼んでしまった直後の弁解。
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds more like Keisuke's earnest, slightly clueless explanation?

choices.text: A: だって、妻のママは、僕にとってもママですから。
B: 配偶者の母は、法律上わたくしの義母に該当いたしますので。

feedback.correct_en: A matches Keisuke's warm, 'ママ' repetition — sincere but tone-deaf — which is exactly why the mother sighs that he doesn't get it.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is dry legalese; it would make Keisuke sound coldly technical rather than endearingly oblivious, undercutting the scene's humor.

contrast_examples.jp: 妻のママは、僕にとってもママですから。
contrast_examples.en: Because my wife's mom is my mom too! (warm, naive)

contrast_examples.jp: 妻の母は、私の義母にあたります。
contrast_examples.en: My wife's mother corresponds to my mother-in-law. (clinical)

prompt.context_jp: 疲れて帰ってきた母に、万理華がおずおずと話しかける場面。
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds more natural from a child begging her mother for a moment?

choices.text: A: 少しだけでいいから、聞いてくれない？
B: 少々お時間を頂戴できますでしょうか。

feedback.correct_en: A is natural child-to-parent pleading: casual plain form with the softening 〜てくれない？ invitation. It conveys both urgency and intimacy.
